policy.aslr: disabled: every tool runs under `setarch x86_64 -R`
policy.argv: relative (-game game <map>.vmf|.bsp) from the map directory
policy.vrad: -ldr then -hdr on the same BSP (the Linux port rejects -both)
policy.dispinfo_mask: DISPINFO bytes VBSP never writes are masked: CDispSubNeighbor orientation/span/neighbor-span after m_iNeighbor 0xFFFF, CDispCornerNeighbors slots >= m_nNeighbors, struct padding

box_light.exercises: sealed box room, one point light: baseline geometry, vis and direct light

disp_occluder.exercises: power-3 displacement hump between a point light and a floor of two sewn power-2 displacements: displacement geometry, neighbors, disp lightmaps, and shadow rays that cross displacement triangles

three_rooms.exercises: three rooms on a dogleg corridor with func_detail crates: real VVIS flow, rooms A and C mutually hidden

sky_spot.exercises: light_environment through a skybox chimney plus a light_spot: sun, sky ambient and cone falloff

verdict.conclusion: identical output; the changed functions are never executed (0 hits) while displacement rays are traced, so the fix removed undefined behaviour in unreachable code only

vrad_uninitialized_read.method: manual, 2026-09-25: valgrind 3.27.1 --track-origins=yes on the post-fix vrad -threads 1 -ldr, sky_spot policy VVIS output
vrad_uninitialized_read.observed: Conditional jump or move depends on uninitialised value(s) at BuildSupersampleFaceLights (utils/vrad/lightmap.cpp), 'Uninitialised value was created by a stack allocation' in BuildSupersampleFaceLights; no other uninitialised-value context in the run
vrad_uninitialized_read.hypothesis: its stackalloc'd pSampleIntensity holds one value per lightmap texel, but ComputeSampleIntensities writes only texels that carry a sample; ComputeLightmapGradients reads all eight neighbours, so the gradient >= 0.0625 supersampling decision can depend on stale stack bytes (pointer values under ASLR, the previous work item's frame with several workers). Consistent with the study: -noextra output is identical across ASLR and 1/4/32 threads. Not fixed here: the gate records legacy bytes, and changing VRAD is a versioned decision.
